jobs.title: Lead Solutions Engineer
jobs.descriptionHtml:
Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, Booking.com, H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

As Lead Solutions Engineer, you will own the technical relationship with Imprint's enterprise partners, ensuring seamless integration, launch, and enhancements of payment solutions. This is a mission-critical role that sits at the intersection of major enterprise partner delivery and internal product strategy, requiring both deep technical expertise and strong business judgment.

You will act as the strategic technical partner to large enterprise partners: managing complex partner solutions that are delivered over many months, translating partner requirements into actionable solutions, driving repeatable launch processes, and ensuring Imprint's platform meets partner needs while staying true to Imprint’s vision to be the best way to pay.

This role blends hands-on technical execution with systems-building, requiring someone who can bring order to ambiguity and scale partner success as Imprint grows.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • You can independently run technical discovery, solution design, and implementation for enterprise partner opportunities.

  • At least one partner implementation is launched through your technical leadership.

  • Clear opportunities to automate partner delivery are identified, prioritized, and at least one automation improvement is shipped or in-flight.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with sales, account management, and product teams to ensure major enterprise partner success from pre-sales through long-term partnership

  • Drive pre-sales technical discovery and solutioning:

    • Understand partner needs and constraints.

    • Map Imprint capabilities to partner requirements.

    • Serve as payments and card program expert to architect a best-in-class card program.

    • Provide technical guidance, architecture input, and implementation approach.

  • Own post-sales technical implementation and partner delivery:

    • Lead integration planning and execution.

    • Troubleshoot technical issues and unblock launches.

    • Build strong relationships with partner technical teams.

    • Drive proactive communication with partners to surface opportunities and mitigate risks.

  • Partner closely with Product and Engineering to influence roadmap:

    • Help define new products and improvements that solve real partner and consumer problems.

    • Ensure new partner and consumer-facing product features are aligned with partner expectations

  • Automate and standardize partner delivery:

    • Improve tooling, documentation, and repeatable integration patterns.

    • Contribute to operational stability at launch time by implementing flexible but repeatable frameworks.

  • Improve technical documentation and partner-facing implementation guides.

Qualifications

Required

  • Experience in solutions engineering, implementation engineering, sales engineering, or similar technical client-facing roles

  • Strong technical background in REST APIs, front-end technologies, and mobile/web SDKs

  • Payments experience is essential: deep understanding of payment networks, PSPs, and payment product architecture

  • General understanding of how products are built, including front-end and back-end development concepts

  • Demonstrated ability to operate effectively in ambiguity and bring structure to unstructured problems

  • Extremely detail-oriented with a track record of managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects to successful completion

  • Collaborative team player with strong cross-functional partnership skills

  • Excellent judgment in balancing partner needs with internal priorities and knowing when to escalate strategic decisions

  • Motivated by building a successful company and willing to operate as a senior individual contributor

  • Proven track record of improving processes through tooling and automation.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with B2B2C partner implementations.

  • Familiarity with data flows, identity/KYC concepts, or risk/compliance considerations in financial products.

  • Familiarity with AI/LLM tools and automation in technical workflows

  • Track record of working effectively in small, high-performing teams

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

Who We Are

Imprint helps the world's best brands grow the lifetime value of their customers. We started with co-branded credit cards and rebuilt them to be smarter, more rewarding, and brand-first. We partner with companies like Crate & Barrel, Rakuten, Booking.com, H-E-B, Fetch, and Shell to launch modern credit programs that deepen loyalty, unlock savings, and drive growth. But the card is just the beginning. We combine advanced payments infrastructure, intelligent underwriting, and deep customer data to create delightful and personalized experiences for members as well as efficient and profitable relationships for our brand partners. Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

Engineering leadership is the lever for this next stage. As Imprint expands into new financial products, launches new brand partnerships, and scales the infrastructure underneath all of it, the quality of our engineering teams determines the quality of everything we ship. AI has made execution faster; the differentiator is the judgment to decide what to build, how to sequence it, and when to say no. That judgment, applied to how teams are built, how they make decisions, and how they're managed, is what Senior Engineering Managers own.

The Opportunity

  • Bring structure to complex, ambiguous domains: Imprint's products sit at the intersection of payments, credit, compliance, and brand strategy. You'll lead a team through problems that aren't fully scoped, where the right answer requires synthesizing technical constraints with product, legal, and financial realities.

  • Operate as a true cross-functional partner: Not just "align with product." You'll work directly with product, compliance, legal, capital markets, and solutions engineering on decisions where the lanes overlap significantly. You will help represent Engineering in the room when strategy is set.

  • Lead with technical credibility, amplified by AI: AI has collapsed the distance between management and IC work. Managers at Imprint use AI tools to investigate codebases, assess the complexity and viability of work, and bring clarity to ambiguous asks. You don't need to be on the critical path writing code (though some managers are), but you need real technical judgment and the modern tools to exercise it.

  • Build and develop a team as a craft: You have a real philosophy on how to hire, develop, and retain strong engineers. You have opinions on how work is scoped and delivered, how to balance short and long-term priorities, and how to give feedback that actually changes outcomes. Clear communication, written and verbal, is key.

  • Operate in the details: This is not a role where technical context and project management are abstracted to other roles or organizational layers. You define the roadmap, scope the work, and manage individuals to outcomes. Even if you've led multiple teams before, the question is: can you take a new team and run it end-to-end?

  • Own outcomes at a company in a defining growth moment: Imprint is growing rapidly, launching new products, and deepening our platform. You'll have the scope and autonomy to shape how your team builds, and your work will be visible in the trajectory of the business.

Your Profile

  • 5+ years of engineering management experience, with a track record of building, developing, and retaining strong engineering teams

  • You've managed through periods of rapid growth, ambiguity, or significant technical change, and your teams came out stronger

  • A strong technical foundation: you were a strong engineer before moving into management, and you've maintained technical credibility through hands-on engagement or modern AI tools

  • You've managed Staff-level ICs and helped senior engineers grow into bigger roles

  • Experience in domains with real complexity: financial systems, distributed infrastructure, regulated environments, or similarly demanding technical areas

  • You communicate with clarity and directness in writing, in 1:1s, in rooms with executives, and in rooms with engineers

  • You drive delivery through your team, not around them. You know how to scope work, set priorities, and create the conditions for engineers to do their best work

  • Experience using AI tools to stay close to technical work (investigating codebases, assessing feasibility, bringing clarity to asks), or genuine enthusiasm to adopt them

Some of our teams are full-stack (frontend, backend, and mobile); others are backend-focused. We're looking for strong engineering leaders regardless of your specific technical background.

We don't expect every candidate to match every bullet. If you're excited about what we're building and confident you can contribute, we'd love to talk.

Stack

Our backend runs on Go, MySQL, DynamoDB, Temporal, Kafka, Kubernetes, and AWS.

Read more about how we build at Imprint on our engineering blog.

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

About You

You've owned CX quality at a contact center scale of 200+ agents (in-house or BPO), built a QA framework from rubric through calibration, and shipped training programs that measurably moved agent performance. You're equally comfortable in a Looker dashboard and a Zendesk Guide CMS. You've worked alongside or implemented an AI deflection product (Sierra, Ada, Decagon, Forethought) and can speak credibly about what makes AI-mediated support actually work.

Role Summary

As Senior Manager of CX Enablement, you will own the quality, training, and knowledge management systems that power Imprint's customer experience. This is a strategic leadership role combining QA framework design, AI-powered deflection enablement, knowledge base ownership, and agent training excellence.

You will drive the architecture that connects quality inputs to AI systems (Sierra), knowledge management, and training outputs—ensuring content quality compounds rather than degrades as Imprint scales. You'll partner closely with engineering, ops, product, and vendor teams to transform customer support from reactive to proactive through automation, rigorous quality frameworks, and data-driven training strategies.

This role reports directly to the Director of Customer Operations and manages a small team of 2–3 associates focused on execution and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Completed a comprehensive knowledge base audit with defined ownership model between CS, engineering, and ops, including refresh SLAs in Zendesk

  • Designed and shipped a new QA framework that moves from manual contact center approaches to fully automated quality scoring with clear expectations

  • Established Sierra AI deflection enablement system with daily feedback loops, gap detection, and content optimization for AI ingestion and delivery

  • Built a scalable partner launch QA and training strategy and applied it to an active launch with measurable quality improvements over prior launches

  • Created a structured training rehaul plan in collaboration with our outsourcing partner, focusing on strategic oversight and outcome monitoring

  • Established trusted partnerships with key cross-functional stakeholders including vendor ops, AI product team, partner success, compliance, and legal

Responsibilities

  • Own the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality management frameworks that drive consistent agent performance across omnichannel support

  • Lead knowledge base strategy and operations in Zendesk, including content audits, ownership models, refresh cadence, and optimization for both human agents and AI consumption

  • Drive Sierra AI deflection strategy by analyzing feedback data, identifying content gaps, optimizing knowledge for LLM ingestion, and improving customer-facing AI delivery

  • Partner with Imprints BPO training teams to design and monitor training programs that address systemic quality issues, leverage AI automation, and scale effectively with new partner launches

  • Build and maintain the technical architecture that connects quality inputs (QA automation, CSAT, sentiment analysis) to training outputs and knowledge base improvements

  • Use data from QM platforms, Sierra AI, and CSAT to diagnose root causes of quality issues—differentiating agent behavior from systemic or content gaps

  • Lead partner launch readiness by designing QA strategies, training plans, and content requirements that prevent launch failures and training debt

  • Establish cross-functional collaboration rhythms with vendor ops, engineering, product, fraud ops, partner success, compliance, and legal teams

  • Manage and develop a team of 2–3 associates responsible for execution, monitoring, and continuous improvement of quality and training operations

Qualifications

Required

  • 7+ years in customer experience, with 4+ years in quality management, training, enablement, or knowledge management roles

  • Experience owning CX quality, training, and enablement at scale (100+ agents, in-house or outsourced), ideally omnichannel

  • Hands-on experience implementing AI-powered deflection projects using tools like Sierra, Ada, Decagon, Forethought, or comparable LLM-based platforms

  • Strong technical fluency with CX platforms such as Salesforce, Zendesk Guide and Support, or comparable knowledge base and support systems (not homegrown tools)

  • Experience with QM platforms such as Maestro QA, Klaus, Playbox, Stella Connect, Tether AI, or similar quality automation tools

  • Exceptional writing skills with the ability to produce compliance-ready content that requires minimal iteration with legal or regulatory teams

  • Data fluency: able to analyze QA trends, CSAT drivers, sentiment data, and agent performance metrics to identify systemic issues vs. behavior gaps

  • Bias toward action and shipping—comfortable building frameworks that get adopted, not just designed

  • Genuine curiosity about how AI is transforming customer service, with a demonstrated commitment to staying at the forefront of CX automation

Nice to Have

  • Experience in fintech, payments, regulated environments, or industries with complex compliance requirements

  • Familiarity with training LMS tools and designing scalable learning programs

  • Background in customer education, support operations, or contact center quality leadership

  • Experience working with outsourced BPO partners and driving adoption of new quality or training standards

  • Track record of redesigning legacy QA or training systems into modern, automated frameworks

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

Role Summary

As Partner Marketing Manager, you will own the full marketing strategy and growth outcomes for several of Imprint's largest co-branded credit card partnerships. You are the marketing leader for your partners: the person accountable for how we acquire, activate, and retain cardholders across every channel, and the person partners look to as the strategic marketing mind behind their program.

  • Created a partner marketing playbook defining audience segmentation, positioning, messaging architecture, and channel strategy that serves as the strategic foundation for internal creative and campaign teams and holds up in senior partner conversations

  • Launched or meaningfully iterated on campaigns in at least two channels (lifecycle, paid social, direct mail, affiliate) with measurable performance improvements and a clear point of view on what to scale next

  • Established yourself as a trusted strategic partner to GMs, Lifecycle Managers, product, engineering, marketing analytics, and partner marketing leadership

  • Demonstrated technical depth in campaign deployment tools and workflows, with the credibility to make architectural decisions about how campaigns are built and delivered

Responsibilities

Marketing Strategy and Growth Ownership

  • Own marketing strategy, planning, execution, and performance for major co-branded partners, with direct accountability for partner growth outcomes including acquisition volume, activation, spend, and retention

  • Lead the development of 12-month marketing roadmaps in partnership with GMs, including quarterly planning cycles, budget allocation, and investment tradeoff decisions

  • Present marketing strategy and performance to partner marketing leadership and internal executives, owning the growth narrative for your assigned programs

  • Identify and prioritize the highest leverage opportunities across the funnel and make investment recommendations based on performance data, partner dynamics, and competitive landscape

Acquisition and Campaign Strategy

  • Design, lead, and optimize acquisition campaigns across paid channels (paid social, paid search, affiliate, direct mail) and owned channels (lifecycle, in-app, email)

  • Make channel mix and budget allocation decisions based on performance data, and have the judgment to shift resources quickly when the data warrants it

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

Role Summary

The Risk team at Imprint is responsible for making smarter, faster credit decisions that balance growth with responsible risk management. The team builds the models, policies, and analytical systems that power underwriting, fraud detection, and portfolio optimization across all of Imprint’s credit programs.

As a Data Scientist, Risk, you will own the modeling powering Imprint’s top-of-funnel credit decisioning—from application intake through approval—across every acquisition channel: direct affiliates (Credit Karma, NerdWallet), invitation-to-apply emails, direct mail, paid social, instant prescreens, and on-site applications. Your primary focus will be improving approval rates while maintaining credit quality: building better underwriting models, designing policy experiments, and uncovering segments where we can safely expand access to credit.

This role sits at the intersection of credit and acquisition strategy. You will partner directly with Credit Strategy, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to build targeting models for new channels, evaluate channel-level credit performance, and connect acquisition volume to downstream economics—approval rates, vintage loss forecasts, LTV, CAC, and contribution profit. Increasingly, that means building not just analyses but AI-powered systems that can autonomously monitor approval rate, channel performance, diagnose shifts, and recommend policy adjustments.

The Opportunity

  • Own and improve the full top-of-funnel credit decisioning pipeline: application scoring, policy rules, decline waterfalls, and approval rate optimization across direct affiliates, invitation-to-apply, direct mail, paid social, instant prescreens, and on-site applications

  • Build and iterate on underwriting, targeting, and segmentation models that expand safe approvals and improve channel-level acquisition quality

  • Design and analyze A/B tests and champion/challenger experiments on credit policies, establishing a test-and-learn cadence with structured readouts on both acquisition and credit performance

  • Build channel-level performance models that connect application volume to downstream economics: approval rates, expected losses, LTV, CAC, and contribution profit

  • Design and build agentic workflows and AI-powered monitoring systems that autonomously detect approval rate anomalies, diagnose score drift and population mix changes, and recommend policy adjustments

  • Partner directly with Credit Strategy, Product, Engineering, and Marketing to develop targeting criteria and risk frameworks for new and emerging acquisition channels

  • Build segmentation frameworks to identify underserved populations where credit access can be responsibly expanded

Your Profile

Required

  • 5 to 8+ years of experience in data science, risk analytics, or a related quantitative field, ideally at a high-growth startup or fintech company

  • Strong Python and SQL skills, with the ability to build models, transform raw data, and create custom datasets from complex financial data

  • Experience building credit risk or targeting models (scorecards, underwriting models, segmentation) or similar predictive modeling in a regulated environment

  • Deep understanding of statistical inference, experimentation design, and causal analysis, with the ability to disentangle policy impact from population shifts and channel mix changes

  • Comfort with AI tools and AI-native workflows; you actively use tools like Claude, Copilot, or similar to accelerate your work and are excited to build AI-powered analytical systems

  • Full-stack problem-solving orientation: you dive into messy data, trace a decline to its root cause, and question assumptions in pursuit of a better answer

  • Ability to present complex findings clearly to technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership and external partner stakeholders

  • Comfort owning projects end-to-end in a fast-moving startup environment with limited scaffolding, collaborating cross-functionally with Policy, Strategy, Product, and Engineering

Nice to Have

  • Experience with credit card underwriting, lending, or consumer credit products

  • Familiarity with credit bureau data (Vantage, FICO, tradeline attributes) and alternative data sources

  • Experience building or scaling experimentation infrastructure for credit policy testing

  • Exposure to fraud detection, KYC/IDV workflows, or application fraud models

  • Understanding of acquisition channel economics and experience partnering with marketing or credit strategy teams on targeting and LTV modeling

We don't expect every candidate to check every box. If this role excites you and you bring strong fundamentals, we encourage you to apply.

Stack

Python and SQL for modeling and analysis. Snowflake for data warehousing. AWS infrastructure. Dashboarding and monitoring tools for production systems.

Learn more about how we build at Imprint on our engineering blog: https://medium.com/imprint-eng

Our robust technology and world-class operations allow us and our brand partners to offer powerful financial products without becoming a bank.

In the U.S., co-branded cards alone account for over $300 billion in annual spend, and most still run on decades-old legacy bank systems. Imprint is the modern alternative: flexible, embeddable, and built for how people actually pay today. Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

Role Summary

As Executive Assistant to the CEO, you will serve as the operational right hand to Imprint's Founder and CEO at a pivotal stage of the company's growth. This is a high-ownership, high-trust role that exists to create meaningful leverage for the CEO by managing complexity, protecting their focus, and ensuring the company's operating rhythm runs without friction.

You will act as a strategic partner and force multiplier — anticipating needs before they arise, making sound judgment calls on behalf of the CEO, and ensuring that nothing falls through the cracks across a fast-moving, high-stakes environment.

This role is based in New York City and requires in-office presence aligned with the CEO's schedule.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Fully owns the CEO's calendar with minimal ramp — making confident prioritization calls independently

  • Established as a trusted gatekeeper and liaison by internal teams, board members, investors, and external partners

  • All board meetings, investor meetings, and partner events run seamlessly with zero logistical gaps

  • Travel logistics are managed proactively with contingency plans in place before they're needed

  • A reliable system exists to track and close every action item and commitment from the CEO's meetings

  • Has identified and implemented at least one meaningful improvement to how the CEO's office operates

Responsibilities

  • Own and optimize the CEO's calendar end to end — balancing internal meetings, board commitments, investor conversations, partner meetings, and protected focus time across multiple time zones

  • Coordinate all logistics for board meetings, investor meetings, and partner events including materials preparation, attendee communications, room setup, travel, and follow-up

  • Manage all domestic and international travel end to end — flights, hotels, ground transportation, itineraries, and backup plans

  • Serve as a trusted gatekeeper and liaison between the CEO and internal teams, investors, board members, and external stakeholders

  • Track and drive closure on action items, commitments, and deliverables that emerge from the CEO's meetings and conversations

  • Support key company moments — all-hands meetings, leadership offsites, major announcements — by owning logistics and ensuring smooth execution

  • Draft emails, messages, and documents on behalf of the CEO that reflect the CEO's voice and standards

  • Proactively identify and implement improvements to how the CEO's office operates — better systems, tools, and workflows that reduce friction and create more leverage

  • Support light personal tasks as needed during high-intensity periods to keep the CEO focused on the business

Qualifications

Required

  • Demonstrated track record of supporting a CEO, Founder, or C-suite executive at a fast-paced, high-growth company — with clear accountability for keeping a complex operation running

  • Experience managing high-volume, high-stakes calendars and travel logistics across multiple time zones

  • Exceptional organizational skills — a proven system for managing complexity and ensuring nothing slips

  • Impeccable judgment and discretion with sensitive, confidential information across all areas of a business

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to draft on behalf of an executive in their voice

  • High ownership orientation — sees what needs to happen and makes it happen without waiting to be told

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity and rapidly shifting priorities; adapts quickly and keeps everything moving

  • Proficiency with modern productivity tools including Google Workspace, Slack, and Notion; ability to quickly adopt new and AI-powered workflows

Nice to Have

  • Experience supporting a CEO through fundraising rounds, board governance processes, or an IPO

  • Familiarity with fintech, financial services, or payments

  • Experience in a company with 100–500 employees during a period of rapid scaling

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Imprint is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Imprint is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

As Manager, Corporate Finance, you will own Imprint's financial planning and analysis function, with direct accountability for building the systems, models, and processes that power forward-looking financial decision-making.

This is a highly technical, hands-on role for someone who builds with code as naturally as they build with spreadsheets — and who is energized by replacing manual workflows with automated, scalable infrastructure. You will partner directly with the Deputy CFO and work cross-functionally with Commercial, Accounting, Treasury, Data and Engineering teams to bring rigor and speed to how Imprint forecasts, plans, and operates financially.

This role is right for someone who thrives in ambiguity, moves fast, and has strong opinions about how modern finance teams should operate.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Migrated major models from Excel to Python, with outputs in Excel or a web-based application, enabling faster iteration and significantly improved accuracy

  • Automated key commentary and data pulls, eliminating manual reporting workflows through Google Sheets, a web application, or equivalent tooling

  • Established a foundation for forward-looking forecasting (3–6 month outlook), including early governance and process structures

  • Built trusted working relationships with Commercial, Finance, Data, and Engineering teams

  • Demonstrated the ability to operate independently and iterate quickly on high-priority workstreams

Responsibilities

  • Own the design, build, and maintenance of Imprint's corporate financial model, transitioning it from Excel to Python-based infrastructure

  • Automate financial reporting and commentary workflows to reduce manual data pulling and accelerate insights delivery

  • Build and maintain forward-looking forecasts (3–6 month horizon) that give the business clear financial visibility

  • Partner with Commercial GMs and partner leads to incorporate revenue and cost inputs into planning models

  • Collaborate with Accounting on book close, cost pipeline, and reporting accuracy

  • Work with Treasury and Vendor Management on cash flow and cost forecasting

  • Support headcount planning and its impact on financial forecasts in partnership with the People team

  • Use AI tooling (e.g., Claude, Cursor) to build scalable, automated finance workflows

  • Identify and eliminate inefficiencies in how financial data is collected, modeled, and reported

  • Present financial insights clearly to senior stakeholders, translating complex outputs into actionable decisions

Qualifications

Required

  • Hands-on, working knowledge of Python — must have built models, scripts, or automated tools, not just theoretical familiarity

  • Demonstrated experience building with AI tools (e.g., Claude, Cursor, or similar) — this is a non-negotiable

  • Background in financial planning, corporate finance, or an adjacent analytical domain

  • Ability to operate with minimal direction and iterate quickly in a fast-moving environment

  • Comfort with ambiguity and a startup mindset — willing to fail fast, course correct, and move forward

  • Strong cross-functional communication skills; able to work effectively with Commercial, Accounting, Treasury, and People teams

  • 5–10 years of experience in a finance, data, or analytically intensive role

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience in fintech, payments, or a product-led company

  • Familiarity with building web-based applications or data pipelines

  • Experience in a high-growth or early-stage company environment

  • Prior exposure to corporate modeling, forecasting, or FP&A processes

Perks & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA

  • 20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents

  • Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Backed by Kleiner Perkins, Thrive Capital, Ribbit, and Khosla Ventures, we're building a world-class team to redefine how people pay and how brands grow. If you want to move fast, solve hard problems, and own real outcomes, we want to meet you.

About the Role

We're looking for a talented, multi-disciplinary Designer to join Imprint's marketing team. Imprint powers co-branded credit card programs for 14+ retail, travel, and lifestyle partners, and this role is at the center of how those brands show up across every customer touchpoint.

This role is for an experienced marketing designer who thrives in high-velocity, multi-stakeholder environments and can manage competing priorities without losing the details.

Key Responsibilities

As a member of the Design Team, you will work collaboratively with Marketing, Product, and Commercial teams across a variety of strategic campaign and lifecycle needs:

  • Design marketing assets across digital, physical, and performance channels for multiple co-branded partner programs, including:

    • Digital: emails, web banners, in-app promotions, push notifications, social posts

    • Performance: landing pages, paid media creatives, promotional campaigns

    • Physical: direct mail pieces, in-store signage, mailers, flyers, postcards — including print production, prepress, and vendor-ready file preparation

    • Brand: partner collateral, presentation templates, co-branded materials

  • Work fluently across multiple partner brand systems and translating creative briefs through each partner's unique guidelines, visual identity, and brand voice

  • Design acquisition landing pages

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams on product and marketing initiatives, managing feedback from both internal stakeholders and external partners

  • Navigate partner review and compliance approval workflows, incorporating feedback from legal, compliance, and partner brand teams

  • Uphold a high bar and own the quality of everything that goes out the door maintaining standards across every partner program

  • Contribute to and maintain design systems and libraries to ensure consistency and scalability across multiple brands

  • Support production workflows including content packaging for translation, asset prep and output, deeplink setup, QR code and UTM generation

Skills and Qualifications

Essential:

  • 5+ years of experience in graphic design and production, ideally supporting multiple brands or product lines simultaneously

  • Strong visual design skills and portfolio of work

  • Deep experience working within and across multiple brand guidelines — comfort managing the cognitive load of switching between distinct brand systems

  • Proficient in Figma (primary design tool), Adobe Creative Suite (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop)

  • Solid understanding of responsive web and mobile design, UX principles, email design, digital advertising, and social media

  • Strong print design and production skills and experience preparing direct mail, signage, and collateral for print, including prepress file preparation and vendor specifications

  • Strong organizational skills and comfort managing multiple concurrent projects

  • Clear, proactive communicator who provides regular updates without prompting and can navigate multi-stakeholder feedback loops (internal teams, external partners, compliance)

  • Extremely responsive working independently in a remote environment

  • Attention to detail, high-quality execution, and ability to prioritize in a fast-moving, high-volume production environment

  • Experience with accessibility standards for web and email (WCAG)

Preferred:

  • Experience in fintech, banking, credit cards, or other regulated industries where legal and compliance review is part of the creative process

  • Familiarity with lifecycle marketing concepts and understanding how design supports acquisition, onboarding, engagement, and retention

  • Experience with or interest in AI-assisted design workflows and maintaining brand quality standards for AI-generated content

  • Experience working with Braze

As General Manager, you are the owner of your business. You’ll sit on one of Imprint’s Partner Success Teams, a small cross-functional pod that brings Revenue, Marketing, and Solutions & Delivery together around a shared portfolio of partners. Within that team, you own the full business outcomes for your partner program, and every Imprint interaction with your partner runs through you.

This is a high-accountability leadership role at the intersection of partner relationship management, P&L ownership, and internal execution. You’ll act as the CEO of your partner program: translating data into strategy, driving top-line growth, building trust with your partner, and keeping the operational rigor your program needs to thrive.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Fully own all partner interactions — the partner knows you as their primary point of contact

  • Become the subject matter expert on your card program, including its unit economics, P&L, and how it contributes to the partner's underlying business

  • Develop a clear, data-backed point of view on how to drive new account growth and existing cardholder spend what is working and what is not, and translate it into a concrete period strategy

  • Stand up and own a rigorous operational cadence with your team to track results, activities, and performance

  • Establish strong internal cross-functional relationships across product, engineering, marketing, risk, credit, and finance

As Senior Data Journalist, you will build Imprint's data storytelling function from the ground up. This is a highly autonomous individual contributor role sitting at the intersection of data science and narrative journalism, the first of its kind at Imprint, and it calls for someone who can operate as a peer to the data science team, not just a consumer of what they hand off.

Working closely with data science, you will independently mine Imprint's payments, merchant, and card member data to surface stories that are credible, data-driven, and genuinely interesting, not promotional. This requires someone who can write production-grade SQL and dbt models themselves, design the analysis with statistical rigor, defend the methodology under scrutiny, and still land the story in clear, compelling prose. You'll set direction independently, hold a narrative strategy under competing priorities, and ship work consistently.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Built and operationalized a data room in partnership with the data science team, including the underlying SQL and dbt models needed to continuously mine and surface story candidates from Imprint's payments, merchant, and card member data

  • Defined the core narrative pillars that will guide Imprint's data storytelling, grounded in the company's brand positioning and differentiated data position, with each pillar mapped to specific, defensible data sources and methodologies

  • Developed an initial content calendar with proposed story formats and publishing cadence, and shipped at least one full story end to end, from raw data to published piece, demonstrating the full workflow

Responsibilities

  • Write and produce data-driven stories that contribute meaningfully to public discourse around how people live and buy today

  • Own Imprint's data storytelling function end-to-end, from writing your own SQL and dbt models to story identification, statistical analysis, and publication

  • Independently design and execute the analytical approach for each story, including sampling methodology, statistical significance, and handling of outliers or data quality issues

  • Partner with the data science team as a technical peer to build and maintain infrastructure for ongoing story mining across Imprint's proprietary data sets

  • Propose and iterate on story formats, publishing cadence, and distribution approach

  • Maintain editorial independence: push back on ad hoc data requests that fall outside the narrative strategy

  • Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, including communications, brand, product marketing, data science, and leadership, to share findings and determine the best ways to distribute stories

Qualifications

Required

  • Demonstrated experience in data journalism, with a portfolio of data-driven stories that combine rigorous quantitative analysis and clear written narrative

  • Advanced SQL and dbt skills, with real production experience building and maintaining data models, not just querying existing ones

  • Working knowledge of statistics, including sampling, significance testing, and how to avoid common pitfalls in observational data, strong enough to defend a methodology under questioning

  • Python or equivalent scripting ability for data transformation and analysis beyond what SQL alone can do

  • Ability to independently QA your own work, build reproducible, version-controlled analyses that are retrospectively defensible if and when questioned, and maintain a high bar for quality and reliability with no analytics team backstopping you

  • Strong writing and the ability to translate complex, technically rigorous data into compelling, accessible stories for a broad audience

  • Track record of working independently to identify, develop, and publish stories without heavy direction

  • Ability to hold a narrative strategy and push back constructively when requests fall outside of it

  • Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast-moving environments where the function, and its technical infrastructure, is being built for the first time

Nice to Have

  • Experience with dbt testing frameworks, data pipeline orchestration, or building analytics infrastructure from scratch

  • Data visualization or graphic design skills

  • Background in economics or applied statistics, or familiarity with consumer finance, payments, or related verticals

  • Experience at a media outlet, think tank, nonprofit, or organization with an established data journalism function

Risk Engineering owns the systems that execute Imprint's risk decisions in real time: transaction authorization and fraud scoring on every card swipe, the underwriting pipeline that evaluates every application, and the vendor integrations that power both. These are latency-sensitive, high-stakes distributed systems with a sprawling surface area and many stakeholders competing for the team's capacity. AI has made execution faster; the differentiator is the judgment to decide what to build, how to sequence it, and when to say no. That judgment, applied to a strong team and a hard domain, is what this Senior Engineering Manager owns.

The Opportunity

  • Own real-time authorization and fraud decisioning: Every card swipe runs through systems your team builds. Decisions happen in milliseconds, failures are visible immediately, and a wrong answer costs real money in either direction: fraud losses on one side, declined good customers on the other. You set the bar for how these systems are designed, tested, and operated.

  • Own the underwriting pipeline: Every application Imprint receives is evaluated by the pipeline your team owns, spanning credit, fraud, identity, and compliance checks. As Imprint launches new brand partners and new products, the pipeline has to absorb new policies and new data sources without becoming brittle.

  • Make vendor decisions that hold up in production: Fraud scoring, identity verification, and bureau data all run through third-party integrations. You'll evaluate vendor capabilities, weigh build-versus-buy with real latency and cost numbers, and push back on approaches that won't survive production load.

  • Prioritize across a wide surface cross-functional surface area: Credit, Fraud, Product, and Compliance all have legitimate asks and compete for the same engineering capacity. You'll bring clarity to poorly-scoped platform problems, decide what the team does and does not take on, and make the reasoning legible to stakeholders who didn't get what they asked for. You define the roadmap and scope the work yourself; nothing is abstracted through organizational layers.

  • Lead with technical credibility, amplified by AI: AI has collapsed the distance between management and IC work. Managers at Imprint use AI tools to investigate codebases, assess the complexity and viability of work, and bring clarity to ambiguous asks. You don't need to be on the critical path writing code (though some managers are), but you need the technical judgment to evaluate design trade-offs on latency-sensitive distributed systems and the modern tools to exercise it.

  • Lead a strong team as a craft: You inherit a strong, psychologically safe team of senior engineers. The job is to keep it that way while raising the ceiling: hand ICs ownership of entire domains, hold the bar on how work is scoped and delivered, and give feedback that changes outcomes. You have a real philosophy on how to hire, develop, and retain strong engineers, and clear written and verbal communication is how you exercise it.

Your Profile

  • 5+ years of engineering management experience, with a track record of building, developing, and retaining strong engineering teams

  • You've managed through periods of rapid growth, ambiguity, or significant technical change, and your teams came out stronger

  • A strong technical foundation: you were a strong engineer before moving into management, and you've maintained technical credibility through hands-on engagement or modern AI tools

  • You've managed Staff-level ICs and helped senior engineers grow into bigger roles

  • You've owned latency-sensitive, high-availability distributed systems in production, where the cost of a wrong decision is measured in real dollars

  • You communicate with clarity and directness in writing, in 1:1s, in rooms with executives, and in rooms with engineers

  • You drive delivery through your team, not around them. You know how to scope work, set priorities, and create the conditions for engineers to do their best work

  • Experience using AI tools to stay close to technical work (investigating codebases, assessing feasibility, bringing clarity to asks), or genuine enthusiasm to adopt them

  • Experience in risk, fraud, underwriting, or payments is a plus

This is a backend team. We don't expect every candidate to match every bullet. If you're excited about what we're building and confident you can contribute, we'd love to talk.

Stack

Our backend runs on Go, MySQL, DynamoDB, Temporal, Kafka, Kubernetes, and AWS. Read more about how we build at Imprint on our engineering blog.

As a trusted people partner to leaders across the business, you’ll build teams where every role matters and people can do the best work of their careers. At the heart of that mission: making Imprint the home of the best managers people will ever work for.

Role Summary

We're looking for a Product Counsel - Data & Privacy to join our legal team as the first-line owner of data, privacy, and information-security legal work. Customer data is core to how Imprint's programs create value, and this role makes sure we share and protect that data the right way, advising on partner data sharing, privacy opt-outs, FCRA and credit data, GLBA/Reg P, data retention, and information security, while working at the pace of a startup that ships fast and takes its regulatory obligations seriously.

This is a high-ownership individual contributor role. You'll act as the first-line legal resource for data-sharing and privacy questions across our ongoing and launching programs. You'll have your own coverage areas from day one, direct access to senior leadership, and real influence on how customer data powers our products. You'll report to our Associate General Counsel and work alongside a small, experienced legal team, partnering closely with our Product Counsel, Data, and Security teams.

This role is ideal for a self-driven attorney who thrives in fast-moving environments, builds strong cross-functional relationships, and takes pride in owning work end-to-end.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Built strong working relationships with Data, Engineering, Security, and Compliance stakeholders.

  • Taken ownership of day-to-day data-sharing and privacy opt-out reviews that require legal sign-off.

  • Provided practical FCRA and GLBA/Reg P guidance on live matters and helped maintain the team's data-sharing and FCRA guides.

  • Advised on data retention questions and at least one partner information-security or incident-response matter.

  • Tracked and closed out legal requests with clear timelines and proactive communication to stakeholders.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the go-to legal advisor on partner data sharing: what customer, account, and application data can be shared through integrations and offline feeds, and on what legal basis, and document that guidance for the Data and business teams.

  • Advise on privacy opt-outs and suppression obligations, including processing partner privacy files and honoring opt-outs across data sets and downstream third parties; maintain business-facing data-sharing and opt-out guides.

  • Provide practical FCRA guidance, including permissible purpose, use and reuse of credit reports, and the sharing of application and credit-decision outcomes.

  • Advise on GLBA / Regulation P and consumer privacy notices, and draft, review, and maintain privacy notices and cardholder information-sharing notices.

  • Interpret state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and emerging state regimes) and automated-decision-making / AI requirements, and advise on their impact on data use, credit scoring, and product design.

  • Own data retention and deletion guidance: mapping regulatory retention obligations and destruction requirements and supporting the record-retention policy.

  • Partner with Security and GRC on partner and vendor information-security risk assessments, testing constraints, and incident response (including forensics, chain of custody, and breach/authority notification).

  • Provide product counseling to Product and Engineering on new features and builds that affect data sharing, privacy, or the customer experience, and draft the consents and data-related terms they need.

  • Coordinate with Compliance on regulatory interpretation, monitoring, and exam preparation, and support the Associate General Counsel on escalated complaints, regulatory inquiries, and bank-partner matters.

  • Translate complex data, privacy, and security requirements into clear, actionable guidance for cross-functional partners.

Qualifications

Required

  • J.D. from an accredited law school and active membership in good standing with at least one U.S. state bar.

  • 4 to 8 years in data privacy law, with demonstrated expertise in GLBA/Regulation P, FCRA, and state privacy laws including CCPA, and consumer financial regulation.

  • Experience in financial services, fintech, or a high-growth startup environment.

  • Working knowledge of FCRA and GLBA / Regulation P, and familiarity with state privacy laws (CCPA/CPRA and newer state regimes) and their practical application to data sharing and product.

  • Experience advising on data-sharing arrangements, privacy notices and opt-outs, and data retention.

  • Strong contract review skills, including data sharing agreements, DPAs, and regulatory-facing documentation.

  • Comfort partnering with security and information-security teams on vendor risk assessments, data protection, and incident response.

  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously, own work end-to-end, manage competing priorities, and deliver clear legal guidance under tight timelines.

  • Strong communicator who proactively updates stakeholders and builds relationships across teams, able to explain a legal risk to an engineer, a data question to an analyst, and a regulatory nuance to a business leader with equal clarity.

  • Willingness to research independently and verify findings with senior team members.

Nice to Have

  • Privacy certification (e.g., CIPP/US).

  • Experience with FCRA in a lending or credit context, ECOA/Reg B adverse action, and automated decision-making / AI governance (e.g., state ADMT laws).

  • Familiarity with data-security frameworks (PCI DSS, SOC 2, NIST) and breach/incident-response processes.

  • Familiarity with additional consumer finance regulations (TILA/Reg Z, EFTA/Reg E, UDAAP, CAN-SPAM, TCPA) and their intersection with data and product.

  • Experience in sponsor bank, banking-as-a-service, or fintech partnership environments.

  • Experience with GDPR applicability and ROPA obligations.

  • Experience working in a ticketing or project management system (e.g., Linear, Jira, Asana).

  • Comfort with legal technology, AI-assisted workflows, and process automation.

  • Experience with consumer credit products, such as credit cards or buy-now-pay-later.

  • Experience building or standardizing privacy frameworks across multiple product lines or partner programs.

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

As Lead Product Marketing Manager (B2B), you will ideate and execute within Imprint's B2B product marketing to drive awareness, adoption and upsells. This is a senior individual contributor role with direct accountability for how Imprint tells its story to partners, prospects, and the market.

You will act as a storyteller and executor for B2B marketing: translating product launches and partnership outcomes into compelling case studies, sales materials, and overall b2b product positioning that makes Imprint's partner-facing narrative come to life.

What Success Looks Like in the First 90 Days

  • Create and iterate on sales collateral and pitch decks reflecting recent product launches

  • Developed long-form case studies in active partnerships

  • Adding to Imprint's new B2B blog including content strategy, structure, and posts

  • Established strong working relationships with Brand, BD, Risk, and GM stakeholders

  • Demonstrated ability to source and shape data-driven narratives independently, without relying on others to surface inputs

Responsibilities

  • Develop and refine assets for B2B organization, including sales collateral like pitch materials, microsites, demos, case studies, and long-form content

  • Support the launch of Imprint's blog, helping to define its voice, cadence, and content strategy in partnership with Brand

  • Translate product launches, partnership outcomes, and risk/data insights into compelling partner-facing narratives

  • Partner closely with BD, Brand, Product, Risk, and Commercial to identify stories worth telling and get the approvals and data needed to tell them effectively

  • Build and run an AI-assisted production system (Claude, design and deck tools) so every prospect and partner gets materials that look and feel custom-made, in a fraction of the time

  • Maintain a modular messaging framework and proof-point library that make fast customization possible without drifting off brand or off compliance

  • Develop deep familiarity with Imprint's business metrics and use data tools (e.g., Snowflake via Claude and MCP integrations) to surface the right inputs for storytelling

Qualifications

Required

  • Demonstrated track record in B2B product marketing, with hands-on experience producing case studies, sales collateral, and long-form content

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication — able to craft convincing, data-informed and technical narratives for a partner and enterprise audience

  • Fintech or regulated industry background — familiarity with what drives B2B partners and how to position around compliance, risk, and product outcomes

  • Proven ability to work independently and self-unblock — comfortable building and moving forward without a fully defined playbook

  • Proficiency in using data to inform storytelling — ability to identify the right metrics, query tools, and translate outputs into narrative

  • Experience running a lean PMM function — able to own outcomes without the support of a large, structured team

Nice to Have

  • Experience at B2B fintech or infrastructure companies

  • Familiarity with co-brand, payments, or card program business models

  • Experience building content programs (blogs, partner hubs, editorial calendars) from scratch

  • Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders including legal, compliance, or risk teams

  • Leading configured work computers of your choice

  • Flexible paid time off

  • Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage

  • Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA
